title: Shelah's Baire-Property Model and Inner-Model Lower Bounds

items.title: Shelah sweetness models for forcing

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: Use the library convention that q≤p means q is stronger. A Shelah sweetness model is a tuple (P,D,(E_n) for n<ω) where P is a forcing preorder, D is dense, each E_n is an equivalence relation on D with countably many classes, E_(n+1) refines E_n, and every E_n-class is downward directed. If p_i∈D for i≤ω and p_i E_i p_ω for every i<ω, then the sequence has a common lower bound; moreover, for every n the tail {p_i:n≤i≤ω} has a common lower bound in the E_n-class of p_ω. Finally, for every p,q∈D and n there is k such that, for every p' E_k p, if some r E_n q satisfies r≤p, then some r' E_n q satisfies r'≤p'. A sweetness model M_2 extends M_1 exactly when P_1 is a complete suborder of P_2 in the maximal-antichain sense (not necessarily dense), D_1⊆D_2, each old E_n is the restriction of the new one, each new E_n-class based at D_1 stays inside P_1, and if p∈D_2 has a stronger q∈P_1 then p∈D_1. Boolean-algebra shorthand retains the original sweetness presentation; transport of equivalence relations is proved only for a specified dense order embedding.
items.proof_plan: Translate Shelah Definitions 7.2 and 7.9 once and for all from the paper's larger-is-stronger order to the library's smaller-is-stronger order. In particular, source upper bounds become library lower bounds. Verify that the displayed conditional transfer clause is exactly source 7.2(d). Also prove the frequently used comparable reformulation: if q≤p, then for every n some k makes each p' E_k p have a common strengthening q' E_n q with q'≤q,p'; conversely, apply that comparable case to the source clause's witness r E_n q to recover the full conditional form. Passing to the separative quotient and regular-open completion preserves compatibility, density, complete embeddings and generic extensions, so all later preorder and Boolean presentations are typed consistently. Do not infer descent of equivalence relations from forcing equivalence. Under a dense order embedding, transport D and E_n bijectively and map original lower bounds to nonzero Boolean elements. Explicitly exclude Boolean zero and the one-element algebra.
items.axiom_base: ZF; no choice principle is used in the definition

items.title: Sweet forcings are countable unions of directed sets and ccc

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: If (P,D,(E_n)) is a sweetness model, then D, and hence P, is a countable union of directed subsets. Consequently every antichain in P is countable, so P satisfies the countable chain condition.
items.proof_plan: Fix n=0. The countably many E_0-classes cover D, and each is directed by the definition. A dense subset that is a countable union of directed sets transfers that decomposition to compatibility witnesses in P. An antichain meets the upward compatibility cone generated by each class in at most one member: two members assigned to one class have extensions into D and then a common extension inside that directed class. Map the antichain injectively into the countable class index. This proves ccc without selecting a representative from every class.
items.axiom_base: ZF; countability is supplied as part of the sweetness witness

items.title: Sweet density transfers along complete suborders

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: Assume ZFC. Let P be a complete suborder of B=BA(Q), let (Q,D,(E_n)) be sweet, and let (A_j)_(j<ω) be subsets of P whose union is dense. For the canonical dense completion map e:Q→B without zero, define p to force q∈Q/P exactly when every P-strengthening of p is compatible with e(q). If q∈D and p∈P forces q∈Q/P, then some j,k have the following uniform property: for every q' E_k q there is p'∈A_j below p which forces q'∈Q/P. Moreover, the union of all A_j for which such a k exists is dense below p.
items.proof_plan: Repeat every j infinitely often as j(i), and use Choice to select q_i E_i q which is bad for A_(j(i)) whenever a bad witness exists. The canonical completion map has dense image and reflects compatibility, so compatibility of p with e(q) yields r≤q in the sweet dense set with e(r)≤p. Transfer and sequential sweetness give a diagonal q* compatible with p. Completeness does not make P dense in BA(Q): instead, if no P-strengthening of p forced q* into the quotient, the P-conditions below p incompatible with e(q*) would be dense. Extend a maximal antichain of those conditions to a maximal antichain of P; maximal-antichain preservation in BA(Q) contradicts compatibility of p and e(q*). Now meet the dense union in one A_j and use a later occurrence j(i)=j to contradict the choice of q_i. Repeating below each p_0≤p proves density of the union of good A_j. Use i+1=2^m(2r+1), including index zero, and Zorn on chain-union-closed antichain posets.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; Choice selects the countable bad-witness sequence and the maximal antichains used in the complete-suborder reduction argument

items.title: Shelah amalgamation preserves sweetness

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
references.locator: Claim 7.3, Lemma 7.5, and Claim 7.12, pp. 34-36 and 41-42

items.statement: Let Q_1 and Q_2 be sweet forcings and let P_0 be completely embedded in BA(Q_1) and BA(Q_2). Their Boolean amalgam Q_1*_(P_0)Q_2 is sweet and contains complete canonical copies of Q_1 and Q_2. If the sweetness model on Q_2 extends a fixed model on Q_1 in the sense of Definition 7.9, the amalgam can be equipped with a sweetness model extending that fixed model. The formulation also permits two named complete embeddings of P_0, by identifying their images before taking the amalgam.
items.proof_plan: Use the pairs admitted by one P_0-condition as the amalgam and retain the same admission witness while applying Claim 7.4 successively in the two coordinates. Define the intrinsic modulus m(x) as the least level at which every coordinatewise equivalent pair is admitted; it carries no selected reduction or witness. Define E_n by equality of m and the two old E_(m+n)-classes. Lemma 7.5 gives density, directedness, the diagonal bound and transfer, while Definition 7.1 gives the two named canonical complete embeddings. For the fixed-model form, use Claim 7.12's separated dense-open presentation D* union D_1 and check all five extension clauses, including the mixed transfer case.
items.axiom_base: ZFC, as required by the full Claim 7.4 supplier and its witness selections

items.title: Shelah's universal-meagre forcing

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
Andrzej Roslanowski and Saharon Shelah, Sweet & sour and other flavours of ccc forcing notions

items.statement: UM has a separately adjoined weakest condition and nontrivial pairs (t,T), with T a nonempty perfect nowhere-dense binary tree and t its initial tree through ht(t). Stronger conditions enlarge T while preserving the recorded initial tree. Over a transitive ZF ground, a generic filter produces a perfect tree whose body is nowhere dense; finite-prefix rearrangements are finite level permutations preserving tails.
items.proof_plan: Verify the two-clause compatibility criterion and fixed-record directed classes by finite unions. Meet the relative height dense sets to include witness trees in U_G. Separately, for each cylinder record a missing extension of its prefix; genericity and directedness permanently exclude it from U_G and prove nowhere density. Use canonical finite codes to inject antichains into omega without Choice. No absorption lemma is used to justify this definition.
items.axiom_base: ZF

items.title: A universal-meagre generic absorbs old nowhere-dense sets

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: Forcing with UM makes the union of all ground-model closed nowhere-dense subsets of Cantor space meagre. Therefore every ground-model meagre set is contained in one meagre set coded by the UM generic.
items.proof_plan: Enlarge an arbitrary nonempty closed nowhere-dense set C to a perfect nowhere-dense set by adjoining fixed perfect binary copies in least cylinders disjoint from C near each cylinder meeting C. Prove closedness and nowhere density by local finiteness outside C, and absence of isolated points directly. Graft all sections of that perfect envelope under one witness node above the recorded height. Meet the dense sets for every old code and for holes in the generic tree. Use the countable prefix-rearrangement envelope; handle the empty set and adjoined weakest condition explicitly.
items.axiom_base: ZF in a transitive ground with a supplied generic; no Countable Choice used.

items.title: Composition with universal-meagre forcing preserves sweetness

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
references.locator: Composition Lemma 7.6, Subclaim 7.8 and Claim 7.11, pp. 36-41

items.statement: Assume ZF+DC. If P has a sweetness model and P forces that Q is UM, then the two-step iteration P*Q has a sweetness model extending that of P. This remains true in the strengthened extension-of-models form used at successor stages.
items.proof_plan: Use the source's dense pairs (p,(t,T)) and enumerate the old equivalence classes A_m. Define E_n by all five of Definition 7.7's interfaces: a sufficiently fine old relation, equality of t, agreement for every m<n of the cone-meeting traces, agreement for every active m<n of the conditional level-n nonmembership decisions, and equality of the finitely many transfer moduli k_m. Subclaim 7.8 stabilizes the data under fine equivalent strengthening. Prove directedness by a common old bound and union of tree names, and prove the sequential clause by Shelah's full block-diagonal avoidance construction. The strengthened fixed-model conclusion is verified separately through Claim 7.11 rather than transported across a bare forcing equivalence. Use total names and the longer target record in the correctly reversed comparable transfer clause; conditional perfect fallback trees justify density.
items.axiom_base: ZF+DC; the source proof uses countable quotient-class enumerations and recursive witness choices

items.title: Continuous countable unions of sweetness models remain sweet

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
references.locator: Definitions 7.2 and 7.9, pp.34 and 40; Claim 7.10, p.41

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let (P_i,D_i,(E_n^i)) for i<δ be a continuous increasing chain of sweetness models, where δ has countable cofinality and every successor extends its predecessor in the exact sweetness-model sense. Then the direct union forcing, dense set, and stabilized equivalence relations form a sweetness model, and every P_i is a complete subforcing of the union. All stages have a common distinguished weakest condition.
items.proof_plan: Choose a fixed increasing cofinal sequence in δ and take the direct unions. Completeness follows directly from the extension definition: every union condition lies in a later stage, where each old maximal antichain is still maximal. The exact class-containment clause makes every union E_n-class meeting an old stage equal to its old class. Countable Choice counts the union of the stagewise quotient classes; directedness occurs in a common later stage. For the sequential clause, all q_i E_i q_omega already lie in the single stage containing q_omega, so apply that stage's clause directly. The same class stabilization reduces the transfer clause to one common stage. Explicitly derive D_j intersect P_i=D_i using an old dense strengthening and the last extension clause; combine this with containment in P_i to stabilize each class. Check the union preorder and density before the sweetness clauses. The common weakest condition remains weakest in the union; without this hypothesis the current extension definition does not ensure a union top.
items.axiom_base: ZF+Countable Choice; CC is used to count the union of the stagewise quotient classes

items.title: Sweet amalgamation extends partial Boolean isomorphisms

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: Let B_0 and B_1 be countably generated complete subalgebras of a sweet complete Boolean algebra B, and let h:B_0→B_1 be a complete Boolean isomorphism. There is a sweet complete Boolean algebra B* containing B completely in which h extends to an automorphism of B*. The extension may be chosen compatibly with any previously fixed sweetness-model embedding.
items.proof_plan: For the one-sided extension, amalgamate the old copy with a disjoint copy over C_1 using the inclusion and the twisted embedding b↦c(g^{-1}(b)); the resulting copy map extends g. Claim 7.12 equips this amalgam with a model extending the old first factor and imposes no extension requirement on the disjoint copy. Alternate that construction with its inverse. The direct union P* is sweet by the continuous-union lemma. The union C of the stage completions is only a Boolean algebra, but the coherent maps form an automorphism of C. Since C is order-dense in BA(P*), Claim 7.13(2) uniquely extends that automorphism to the completion. Sweetness is retained through the dense forcing presentation P*, not transported through an unspecified completion map.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; Choice supplies the countable induction data used in the source construction

items.title: Shelah's CH-length homogeneous sweet construction

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: Assume ZFC and CH. There is a continuous increasing chain of sweetness models P_α for α<ω_1. Put B_α=BA(P_α) and P=union P_α. The B_α form an increasing chain of complete Boolean algebras of size at most ω_1, while the final completion satisfies the special identity B=BA(P)=union B_α, is ccc, and has size ω_1. Every complete isomorphism between countably generated complete subalgebras of B extends to an automorphism of B; every scheduled free-amalgamation task is met; and above every stage a later quotient has the canonical UM presentation.
items.proof_plan: Under CH, enumerate all countable stage data and repeat the isomorphism, free-amalgamation and UM tasks cofinally. Construct a continuous chain of sweet forcing presentations P_α, with B_α=BA(P_α). At a countable limit take P_λ=union P_α and only then complete it; do not identify B_λ with the direct union of the prior completions. Successor tasks use the twisted partial-isomorphism extension, named-embedding amalgamation and canonical UM composition interfaces. Sweetness gives ccc, so CH bounds each completion. At the final union invoke Main Lemma 7.14's special identity BA(union P_α)=union B_α and its union-level clauses directly; the countable-cofinality lemma is not applied at ω_1. For previously extended maps over whole completions use original Claim 7.13 with arbitrary complete subalgebras. Well-order only the task-code sets using AC.
items.axiom_base: ZFC+CH; full AC is used for the global bookkeeping well-order and transfinite recursive choices

items.title: Real names are captured and coded meagre unions are absorbed

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: In the generic extension by the final algebra B, every name for a real, a Borel code, or a countable sequence of ordinals is equivalent to a name over some B_α. Consequently, for every such sequence s, a later UM quotient makes the union of all meagre Borel sets coded in V[s] meagre. When the construction starts over L, the choices made by the generic on the countably many deciding antichains for s are coded by one real, while the ground-model name and antichain enumerations have ordinal codes; hence s is definable from that real and finitely many ordinals.
items.proof_plan: For every coordinate take a maximal deciding antichain; ccc makes it countable, and the countably many Boolean values occur below one stage of the final special union. Completeness preserves maximality and yields a stage name, including for ordinal coordinates. Over L, use its canonical definable well-order to code the ground name, the antichains and their enumerations by ordinals, while one real records the unique generic index chosen in each antichain. Choose a later quotient with the exact canonical UM presentation. Every meagre Borel set coded in V[s] is then old, and the UM absorption theorem puts all such codes into one meagre F-sigma envelope. This uses the construction's actual completion identity and no arbitrary forcing-equivalence substitution.
items.axiom_base: ZFC in the ambient forcing extension; regularity of ω_1 and the ccc name calculation are explicit

items.title: Strongly homogeneous truth has Baire representatives

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
Robert M. Solovay, A Model of Set-Theory in Which Every Set of Reals Is Lebesgue Measurable

items.statement: Let B be the final Boolean algebra of the Shelah construction. For every formula φ(x,s,γ⃗) with a countable ordinal-sequence parameter s and finitely many ordinal parameters γ⃗, the set of reals x for which the B-generic extension satisfies φ(x,s,γ⃗) differs from a Borel set by a meagre set. In particular this holds for real-and-ordinal parameters. The Borel code and meagre-error code belong to the final extension.
items.proof_plan: Capture the parameter in a countably generated complete algebra whose generic extension is exactly V[s]: labelled deciding antichains both recover s and determine the generic trace on a countable dense subalgebra. Free amalgamation over the parameter-and-Cohen algebra forces the formula Boolean value into that algebra. Read it as a Cohen regular-open code and transport it by automorphism extension to every Cohen real over V[s]. Absorb precisely those V[s]-coded nongenericity witnesses using the later canonical UM quotient, then apply Borel-to-open conversion.
items.axiom_base: ZFC in the ambient extension; the conclusion is a statement later internalized in ZF+DC

items.title: The Shelah HOD(S) model and its real-ordinal presentation

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
Robert M. Solovay, A Model of Set-Theory in Which Every Set of Reals Is Lebesgue Measurable

items.statement: For the inner-model branch, start the CH construction over the constructible ground L. In the generic extension let S be the class of all countable sequences of ordinals and define N=HOD(S): every member of the transitive closure is uniquely definable in a rank from one s∈S and finitely many ordinals. Finite and countable lists of S-parameters interleave into one, and every real belongs to N. By the preceding countably-generated-support coding over L, this is precisely the convenient HOD(S) presentation of the hereditary real-and-ordinal model required by Shelah 7.17: every set of reals in N is definable from one real and finitely many ordinals. No equality with L(R), HOD(R), or any class built from all ω_1-sequences is asserted.
items.proof_plan: Rank-bounded satisfaction makes OD(S) and HOD(S) first-order. A fixed pairing on ω interleaves countably many countable ordinal sequences, and a real is itself such a sequence. For the real-and-ordinal presentation, take the B-name for the one S-parameter defining A⊆R. The capture lemma supplies countably many canonically enumerated deciding antichains; one real records the generic's chosen index in each, and V=L gives an ordinal code for the ground-model name and enumerations. Substitute the resulting definition of s into the rank-bounded definition of A. Conversely, a real plus finitely many ordinals interleaves into one member of S. This proves the advertised equivalence in the only branch where it is used and does not claim that an arbitrary countable ordinal sequence is intrinsically real-coded in an arbitrary ground extension.
items.axiom_base: ZF for the class definition

items.title: The Shelah inner model is closed under ambient omega-sequences

references.title: Robert M. Solovay, A Model of Set-Theory in Which Every Set of Reals Is Lebesgue Measurable

items.statement: If f belongs to the ambient ZFC forcing extension and maps omega into N=HOD(S), then f itself belongs to N.
items.proof_plan: Use full definition codes (formula, rank, finite tuple length, tuple, S parameter). Collection bounds the fibres before one ambient AC selection. Encode every field by an explicit row and a fixed pairing; decode a unique function and apply finite reflection with its S parameter. Prove finite-set OD(S) closure and account for the Kuratowski graph transitive closure. The proof works in any ambient ZFC universe for this HOD(S) definition.
items.axiom_base: Ambient ZFC; AC is used only for simultaneous selection of definition codes

items.title: The Shelah inner model satisfies ZF and Dependent Choice

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
Robert M. Solovay, A Model of Set-Theory in Which Every Set of Reals Is Lebesgue Measurable

items.statement: N=HOD(S) is a transitive inner model with the same ordinals and reals as the ambient Shelah extension, satisfies every axiom of ZF, and satisfies the serial-relation form of Dependent Choice.
items.proof_plan: Transitivity, all ordinals, all reals, Extensionality, Foundation, Pairing, Union and Infinity are immediate from hereditary definability. Prove Separation by conjoining fixed definitions; Replacement by defining the image from fixed codes for the function and domain, without selecting a code per value; and Power Set by the uniform OD(S) predicate. For the starting-point-free form of DC, take in N a nonempty A and a serial R on A. Ambient AC chooses an initial point and recursively produces an R-chain. The closure lemma puts that omega-sequence in N, and transitivity makes membership in R absolute. No equivalence with prescribed-start DC is used.
items.axiom_base: The inner conclusion is ZF+DC; ambient ZFC supplies the sequence later internalized by omega-closure

items.title: Every real set in the Shelah inner model has the Baire property

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
Robert M. Solovay, A Model of Set-Theory in Which Every Set of Reals Is Lebesgue Measurable
references.locator: Part III, Sections 1.6 and 2.8-2.10, pp. 42 and 52

items.statement: N satisfies that every subset of the reals has the property of Baire. This is first proved for the set-theoretic real space 2^ω and transferred to the usual real line through comeagre homeomorphic coding subspaces. For each real set A in N there are in N an open set U and a meagre set M in the relevant space such that A symmetric-difference U is contained in M.
items.proof_plan: For A⊆2^ω in N, use its rank-bounded definition and the homogeneity theorem to obtain a Borel representative with coded meagre error. Apply the uniform Solovay code construction to turn that Borel code into an open code plus a coded nowhere-dense error. Same reals puts all codes in N. Prove evaluation agreement locally: ill-foundedness of a countable code would yield a descending real, nodewise well-founded induction makes evaluation absolute, and the finite-cylinder test makes closed nowhere density arithmetic. DC, hence Countable Choice, verifies the displayed union is meagre in N. For the usual real-line convention, pass through the infinitely-many-ones subspace of Cantor space, Baire space and the irrationals; the omitted binary sequences and rationals are countable, so the transported open approximation remains valid modulo meagre sets.
items.axiom_base: ZF+DC inside N

items.title: The exact equiconsistency of ZFC and the all-Baire-property model

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: The following theories are equiconsistent: ZFC; ZFC plus every real set first-order definable from a real and ordinal parameter has the Baire property; and ZF+DC plus every set of reals has the Baire property. In particular, Con(ZFC) is equivalent to Con(ZF+DC+all real sets have BP), with no inaccessible-cardinal hypothesis.
items.proof_plan: Invoke Shelah's published Conclusion 7.17 as the exact equiconsistency theorem. Its forward proof and Theorem 7.16 directly supply the definable-BP full extension; the local inner-model results separately identify HOD(S) as satisfying ZF+DC+all BP. Its reverse proof invokes Gödel's L, matching the library's semantic constructible-inner-model theorem. Do not infer either the full-extension clause from same-real inner-model witnesses or a uniform formal forcing compiler from the construction theorem.
items.axiom_base: Metatheory of formal relative consistency; object-theory conclusions exactly as stated

items.title: Boldface Sigma-one-three measurability

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals
references.locator: Definition 1.17 and Facts 1.17-1.18, pp. 10-11; Chapter 3, Section 3.1, pp. 43-44

references.title: Terence Tao, An Introduction to Measure Theory, Exercise 1.4.26, p. 94

items.statement: For a real parameter x, a subset A of Cantor space is Sigma^1_3(x) when membership has the form: there exists a Baire real y, for every Baire real z, there exists a Baire real w such that an arithmetic predicate of the displayed reals, x, and a natural-number code holds. Boldface Sigma^1_3 measurability means that every Sigma^1_3(x) subset of Cantor space is measurable for completed coin measure for every real x. Sigma^1_2(x) sets are included by a dummy final existential quantifier.
items.proof_plan: Define the arithmetic existential-universal-existential prefix in ZF, retaining Cantor measured carrier and Baire real quantifiers. Under Countable Choice use the Borel coin measure supplied by the dyadic construction after its choice step and form its completion E=B union N, with N contained in a Borel null set, by the measure-completion theorem. Tuple pairing and a dummy quantifier give the indicated coding inclusion.
items.axiom_base: ZF for the pointclass syntax; Countable Choice for the Borel coin measure and completed-measure interpretation.

items.title: Rapid filters and the Raisonnier family

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: A filter F on omega is rapid when it extends the Frechet filter and, for every increasing f:omega→omega, some a∈F satisfies |a∩f(n)|≤n for every n. Equivalently, it is enough that one fixed strictly increasing g uniformly replace n on the right for every increasing f; the Frechet filter then permits deletion of one finite initial segment to recover the exact inequality. For distinct binary reals u,v let h(u,v) be their first differing prefix length (one plus the zero-based first differing coordinate) and H(X)={h(u,v):u,v∈X,u≠v}. For a real x, F(x) is a subfamily of P(omega), and a subset a of omega belongs to F(x) exactly when a countable cover (F_n) of L[x]∩2^omega satisfies the union of all H(F_n) is contained in a.
items.proof_plan: Prove Ishii Lemma 3.6 explicitly. The forward direction takes g(n)=n. Conversely apply the uniform-g hypothesis to f*(n)=f(g(n+1)); for k in [g(n),g(n+1)) use the exact inequality g(n)<=k, then delete the finite set f(g(0)), which preserves filter membership because the Frechet filter is contained in F. Check that first difference exists and that H is invariant under closure by approximating two distinct closure points through their first-difference coordinate. Thus witnessing cover members may be replaced by closed tree bodies. Define F(x) explicitly as a subfamily of P(omega), so the displayed membership variable is always a subset of omega. The filter and rapidity assertions are still proved separately from the definition. Retain Ishii prefix-length convention explicitly, and define the relativized L[x] hierarchy using the real graph predicate.
items.axiom_base: ZF

items.title: The Raisonnier family is a Sigma-one-three filter

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals
references.locator: Lemma 3.8 and the complexity discussion before Theorem 3.12, pp. 46-48

references.title: Thomas Jech, Set Theory, Chapter 25

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and omega_1^{L[x]}=omega_1. Then F(x) is a proper filter on omega extending the Frechet filter, and membership a∈F(x) is a Sigma^1_3(x) property of the real a.
items.proof_plan: Upward closure and finite intersections follow from the cover definition. Canonical least well-order codes inject omega_1^{L[x]} into the constructible reals without simultaneous choice; Countable Choice then rules out a countable singleton cover and proves properness. Cylinder covers give the Frechet filter. For complexity, countable well-founded level certificates make z in L[x] Sigma^1_2(x); a real codes a sequence of binary trees, and the coverage clause quantifies only z in 2^omega, exactly matching the domain L[x] intersect 2^omega in the definition. That clause is Pi^1_2(x), and its first-difference clause is Pi^1_1, so existentially quantifying the tree code gives Sigma^1_3(x). Well-order codes include a domain subset of omega, so finite and zero ordinals are represented as well as infinite countable ordinals.
items.axiom_base: ZF+Countable Choice; no GCH cardinality shortcut is used

items.title: Rapid filters are not Lebesgue measurable

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: Every rapid filter on omega, regarded through characteristic functions as a subset of Cantor space with coin measure (and hence through the standard coding as a real set), is not Lebesgue measurable.
items.proof_plan: A measurable filter extending the Frechet filter is invariant under finite changes. The tail zero-one law and the complement map make it null. To contradict nullity, first fix an arbitrary closed positive set B. Recursively choose finite string families T_i at increasing lengths so B is almost covered by their cylinders and every conditional B-density above a member of T_i exceeds 1-2^{-(i+2)}; choose them canonically using the density theorem. Rapidity supplies a in F sparse at the level bounds n_i. Inductively choose nested s_i in T_i and points of B satisfying value 1 on the sparse coordinates: independence gives measure strictly above the uncovered error. The union b lies in closed B and contains a, hence b belongs to F. Thus F meets every closed positive set and has positive outer measure, contradicting nullity.
items.axiom_base: ZF+Countable Choice; CC is declared directly because the published Lebesgue density theorem consumes it

items.title: A measurable null-code order bounds the constructible null union

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals
Thomas Jech, Set Theory, Chapter 25

items.statement: For a real x define A(x) on pairs (u,v) by comparing the least canonical L[x] null G-delta codes containing u and v. Then A(x) is Sigma^1_2(x). Under Countable Choice, if A(x) is measurable, the union G of all null Borel sets coded in L[x] is null in the ambient universe.
items.proof_plan: Relativize the canonical definition-code order to L[x]. A well-founded countable-level certificate, obtained by a canonical Skolem hull, is Pi^1_1 and exactly enumerates each real-code predecessor segment. Define the strict order A(x) only on G times G by witnessing a code below the first code of v that contains u but not v. This gives Sigma^1_2(x). Every horizontal section is a countable union of coded null sets. Tonelli and completed Fubini make A(x) product-null and give a null exceptional set for vertical sections; either G lies in it or one good u splits G into its lower section, one null layer, and its upper section.
items.axiom_base: ZF+Countable Choice; the relative L[x] certificates use canonical witnesses, and completed Fubini is used exactly once

items.title: Uniform null G-delta sets capture block functions

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals
Terence Tao, An Introduction to Measure Theory
references.locator: Outer measure and the Caratheodory construction, Chapter 1

items.statement: There are uniformly assigned null G-delta sets N_f in Cantor space for f in omega^omega and, for each open U whose canonical coin content is below one, finite capture sets φ_U(n) of size at most 2^(n+1), such that N_f⊆U implies f(n)∈φ_U(n) for all sufficiently large n. If f belongs to a transitive model, the code for N_f belongs to that model.
items.proof_plan: Construct coin content directly from prefix-free cylinder codes in ZF. Finite binary-pattern counts give the block contents and independence products. Remove every zero-content basic trace from the positive closed complement of U using canonical finite covers with summable errors. Tail content estimates prove N_f null directly. Independence bounds the weighted missed-block sets A_s; canonical thresholds and least witnesses give the finite slaloms with the sharp size bound. The ZF Baire theorem on the remaining closed separable complete set yields eventual capture.
items.axiom_base: ZF; canonical least choices and the complete-metric Baire theorem avoid an unstated choice principle

items.title: Uniform null-code measurability makes the Raisonnier filter rapid

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals
Spyridon Dialiatsis and Yurii Khomskii, Combinatorial Properties of the Raisonnier Filter

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and omega_1^{L[x]}=omega_1. If the null-code order A(x join r) is measurable for every real r, then the Raisonnier filter F(x) is rapid; boldface Sigma^1_2 measurability is a sufficient uniform hypothesis.
items.proof_plan: For arbitrary increasing block endpoints n_i, code the sequence by r and work in M=L[x join r]. Uniform measurability and the null-code lemma make the union of M-coded null Borel sets null. Put it inside a Borel null hull; inner regularity of the complement yields one open U of measure below one. Apply the uniform capture lemma to every M-real's prefix function. The countable classes of reals sharing an initial prefix and captured at all later levels cover M, while their first differing prefix lengths lie in a set a assembled in the blocks (n_(i-1),n_i]. Finite binary prefix trees give |a intersection n_i| below the fixed exponential bound, and the uniform-bound criterion makes F(x) rapid.
items.axiom_base: ZF+Countable Choice; CC enters through the two preceding filter/null-code lemmas

items.title: Failure of inaccessibility in L produces a real with correct omega-one

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: Work in ZF+Countable Choice. If the ambient omega_1 is not an inaccessible cardinal of L, then there is a real x such that omega_1^{L[x]} equals the ambient omega_1.
items.proof_plan: Countable Choice makes ambient omega_1 regular. It is a cardinal and regular in L because any contrary L map remains a contrary map in V. If it is not inaccessible in L, GCH in L therefore makes it (mu^+)^L for an infinite L-cardinal mu<omega_1; do not claim that mu remains a cardinal in V. The ordinal mu is ambient-countable, so choose one real x coding a bijection omega→mu. The zero ordinal is countable trivially. For every nonzero beta<(mu^+)^L, Choice in L gives a surjection mu→beta, which remains in L[x]; composing with x makes beta countable in L[x]. Thus omega_1^{L[x]} is at least ambient omega_1, while ambient omega_1 remains uncountable in the inner model because any L[x] bijection would exist in V. Hence equality. Only this existential x is retained.
items.axiom_base: ZF+Countable Choice; CC supplies regularity of ambient omega_1 and the enumeration of the countable α

items.title: Sigma-one-three measurability makes omega-one inaccessible in L

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: Assume ZF+Countable Choice and boldface Sigma^1_3 measurability. Then the ambient omega_1 is an inaccessible cardinal in L.
items.proof_plan: Suppose not and obtain x with omega_1^{L[x]}=omega_1. For every real r, A(x join r) is Sigma^1_2(x join r), hence Sigma^1_3(x join r) and measurable by the boldface hypothesis. This verifies the repaired rapidity theorem's uniform premise, so F(x) is rapid. Its complexity lemma makes it Sigma^1_3(x), while the rapid-filter theorem makes it nonmeasurable, a contradiction.
items.axiom_base: ZF+Countable Choice; no full AC

items.title: All-real-set measurability yields an inaccessible inner model

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: If a universe satisfies ZF+DC and every set of reals is Lebesgue measurable, then its constructible universe L satisfies ZFC and contains an inaccessible cardinal—indeed the ambient omega_1 is inaccessible in L. This item asserts the semantic inner-model conclusion, not an arithmetized consistency implication.
items.proof_plan: DC implies Countable Choice by the published implication theorem. Universal measurability implies boldface Sigma^1_3 measurability, so the exact lower-bound theorem makes ambient omega_1 inaccessible in L. The constructible inner-model schema gives all ZF axioms internally and the canonical constructible well-order gives AC, hence L satisfies ZFC; the large-cardinal definition verifies that the same ordinal is uncountable, regular and strong limit there. The proof stops at that semantic conclusion because the cited inner-model schema explicitly supplies no arithmetized consistency transfer.
items.axiom_base: ZF+DC in the source model; L satisfies ZFC plus an inaccessible cardinal

items.title: Exact equiconsistency of universal measurability and an inaccessible

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: ZFC plus an inaccessible cardinal and ZF+DC plus every set of reals Lebesgue measurable are equiconsistent. The same lower bound already follows from universal boldface Sigma^1_3 measurability under Countable Choice.
items.proof_plan: For the upper bound invoke the published external finite-fragment consistency theorem for the Solovay Levy-collapse construction; do not invoke a conditional uniform forcing compiler. For the universal-measurability lower bound, the preceding theorem supplies a definable constructible inner model of ZFC with an inaccessible, and interpretation transports any actual target refutation back to the source. For the stronger Countable-Choice plus boldface Sigma^1_3 lower bound, use the exact inaccessible-in-L theorem and the same interpretation argument.
items.axiom_base: Metatheory of relative consistency; exact object theories are stated in both directions

items.title: Shelah's model separates universal Baire property from universal measurability

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: Relative to Con(ZFC), it is consistent that ZF+DC holds, every set of reals has the Baire property, and not every set of reals is Lebesgue measurable. Thus universal Baire property does not entail universal Lebesgue measurability over ZF+DC.
items.proof_plan: Use first-order completeness to take a countable, possibly externally ill-founded model M of ZFC. Internally choose L^M if it has no inaccessible, or the L^M-rank segment at its least inaccessible; the internal rank-segment and constructibility theorems give a ZFC+V=L+no-inaccessible model N_0. Apply the direct CH sweet-construction theorem inside N_0, rather than treating equiconsistency as a forcing interface, and externally meet the countably many internal dense sets, forming the extension as the Boolean-valued quotient of internal names. The local HOD(S) theorems give ZF+DC+all BP. The internal forcing theorem proves that set forcing preserves the internal ordinals and L-levels, and the transitive same-ordinal inner model HOD(S) therefore has L equal to N_0. If every real set there were measurable, DC gives Countable Choice, noninaccessibility supplies x with correct omega_1, and measurability of every A(x join r) makes F(x) rapid, contradicting rapid-filter nonmeasurability.
items.axiom_base: Relative consistency over ZFC; the final inner model satisfies ZF+DC

title: Shelah's Baire-Property Model and Inner-Model Lower Bounds: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A universal-meagre stage absorbs an old nowhere-dense tree

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: For every old perfect nowhere-dense binary tree S and UM condition (t,T), the absorption lemma gives a direct extension whose generic F-sigma code contains [S]. If some level beyond t satisfies |T_n|≥|S_n|, the finite graft is explicit; this always covers the singleton {0^omega} instance.
items.proof_plan: For the matched-width case replace each old section prefix by its distinct target node, appending only tails and closing under prefixes. Use full level permutations to recover branches, and assign each one its least index in the absorption lemma's fixed canonical enumeration before naming the finite subunion. For the singleton use the explicit perfect tree with even coordinates zero and odd coordinates free, grafted under one node. Use ht(t) and refine the adjoined weakest condition first. General absorption is supplied by the repaired absorption lemma.
items.axiom_base: ZF

items.title: Cylinder covers generate the Frechet tails in the Raisonnier filter

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: For fixed n, enumerate the finitely many length-n binary strings s and use their cylinders [s] as a countable cover of L[x]∩2^omega. Any two distinct reals in one cylinder first differ at a coordinate at least n, so their first differing prefix length is at least n+1. Hence omega minus n belongs to F(x), concretely demonstrating that F(x) extends the Frechet filter.
items.proof_plan: List all 2^n strings and pad the finite list by empty sets to an omega-sequence. Every binary real extends exactly one listed string. If u and v lie in the same cylinder they agree below n, so the first differing coordinate is at least n and the prefix-length convention gives h(u,v)≥n+1; therefore the union of all H([s]) is contained in the cofinite tail of integers at least n. Apply the defining cover criterion. Check n=0 separately: every distinct pair in the one empty-string cylinder has prefix length at least one, and the witness gives omega itself.
items.axiom_base: ZF

items.title: Uniform null capture for a constant block function

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: For the constant function f(n)=0, the uniform capture lemma assigns a null G-delta set N_f. Whenever an open U of measure below one contains N_f, the associated finite capture sets satisfy 0∈φ_U(n) for all sufficiently large n.
items.proof_plan: Instantiate the exact uniform-capture theorem at the constant function f(n)=0. Its first conclusion supplies the null G-delta N_f. Under N_f⊆U, its capture conclusion gives f(n)∈φ_U(n) eventually, which specializes to 0∈φ_U(n) eventually.
items.axiom_base: ZF

items.title: False: the all-Baire-property model needs an inaccessible

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: False: an inaccessible-cardinal hypothesis is needed as an upper-bound assumption to establish the relative consistency of ZF+DC plus universal Baire property. Con(ZFC) already implies the consistency of that theory, whereas universal Lebesgue measurability is equiconsistent with an inaccessible. This does not assert the separate metatheoretic negation of Con(all BP) implying Con(ZFC+inaccessible).
items.proof_plan: Fix the refuted reading as the alleged need for an inaccessible hypothesis in the relative-consistency construction. The Baire-property theorem gives Con(ZFC) implies Con(ZF+DC+all BP), directly refuting that need. Contrast this with the exact measurability equiconsistency theorem. The separation theorem supplies a single relative model satisfying all BP but not all measurability, so the regularity assertions separate semantically. Explicitly do not infer from equiconsistency with ZFC that Con(all BP) cannot imply Con(ZFC+inaccessible), and do not transfer the measurability lower bound to BP.
items.axiom_base: Metatheory of relative consistency

items.title: Amalgamating two sweet models over a common complete subalgebra

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
references.locator: Claim 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, printed pp. 35-36; Claims 7.12-7.13 and Main Lemma 7.14, printed pp. 41-43

items.statement: Let (P_1,D_1,E^1_n) and (P_2,D_2,E^2_n) be sweetness models whose complete Boolean algebras share a common complete subalgebra B_0. Then the admitted-pair amalgam P_1*_{B_0}P_2 is sweet, has complete canonical embeddings of both factors, and is ccc.
items.proof_plan: Apply the exact named-embedding amalgamation theorem over the arbitrary complete subalgebra. On the dense admitted pairs use the intrinsic least modulus m(x), defined by admission of every coordinatewise E_m-perturbation and carrying no chosen witness. The shifted coordinate classes supply the sweetness clauses, the theorem supplies complete canonical copies, and sigma-directedness supplies ccc. No countable-generation, partial-isomorphism or CH-length hypothesis is used.
items.axiom_base: The choice cost is inherited from the amalgamation and density-transfer suppliers; no CH-length construction is invoked.
